newsitem.title: USA: General Mills Q3 domestic food volume down.
newsitem.headline: General Mills Q3 domestic food volume down.

text.p: General Mills Inc said Wednesday that its domestic retail packaged food volume dropped one percent in the fiscal third quarter, contributing to a one percent decline in total sales to $1.29 billion.
General Mills, the number two U.S. cereal maker, said sales were also hurt by lower cereal prices implemented in June 1996.

The company said its Big G cereal division saw a three percent drop in unit volume in the third quarter, reflecting the shift of some volume into the second quarter when cereal volume grew more than 10 percent.
It also cited lower promotional spending levels versus the prior year.

Analysts had expected General Mills to report lower cereal volume in the third quarter ended February 23. It reported net earnings for the quarter of $0.78 a share, up from $0.73 a year ago, meeting the First Call consensus.

For the first nine months of fiscal 1997, Big G volume was up four percent, which General Mills said outpaced the ready-to-eat cereal category's one percent growth in all outlets. It said Big G's market share, excluding recently acquired cereal brands, rose nearly one point to 24 percent.
Adding in the cereal brands acquired from Ralcorp Holdings Inc, General Mills has roughly a 27 percent market share.
General Mills also said its third quarter unit volume drop reflected the impact of two less shipping days in the period due to holiday timing.

Chairman Stephen Sanger said General Mills' results for the first nine months keep it on pace to deliver record earnings per share in fiscal 1997. In an interview last month, Sanger told Reuters he expected record earnings, record volume and record market share for fiscal 1997.

"The first half of this year was characterized by above-trendline six percent unit volume growth, but earnings were essentially flat because they included the majority of the impact from Big G's cereal price declines," Sanger said in a statement.
General Mills earned $2.40 after an $0.18 charge in the first nine months, compared with $2.51 a year ago.

"Our third-quarter results show just the reverse -- domestic volume was down slightly but earnings were up, reflecting lower levels of marketing activity versus the prior year and the full implementation of expense reductions made in conjunction with the cereal price declines," Sanger added.
He added that the company expects unit volume growth to resume in the fourth quarter. "The strength of that volume increase will be the key factor determining our annual earnings gain," Sanger said.

General Mills added that unit volume for its international operations was up eight percent for the third quarter and through the nine months. Cereal Partners Worldwide, its joint venture with Nestle SA, led international volume performance with 18 percent gains in the third quarter and nine months.
